chunk_1.page_content:
# 1 Introduction

This Interface Requirements Specification (IRS) defines five illustrative application-level packet formats exchanged between independent subsystems. Each packet definition identifies its sender, receiver, flow direction, field layout, encoding, and validation requirements. The examples are intentionally varied and are designed to exercise automated extraction and packet-pattern detection; they do not represent a production system.

chunk_2.page_content:
## 1.1 Purpose

This document provides packet definitions that can be extracted into a machine-readable representation and used to locate and validate packet occurrences within captured network traffic.

chunk_3.page_content:
## 1.2 Scope

This IRS specifies packet structures and interface-level validation. It does not prescribe routing, retransmission, or transport connection management.

chunk_5.page_content:
## 2.1 Subsystem and Flow Direction

Each packet definition identifies an originating subsystem (Sender) and destination subsystem (Receiver). Direction is written Sender → Receiver. The sender constructs the packet; the receiver validates and interprets it. A packet observed in the reverse direction shall not be treated as the same packet type unless explicitly specified.

chunk_6.page_content:
## 2.2 Byte Numbering and Alignment

Offsets are zero-based from the first byte of the application-level packet. Fields are serialized in table order. Every field occupies a whole number of bytes. This IRS contains no bit-packed fields.

chunk_7.page_content:
## 2.3 Boolean Representation

Every Boolean field occupies exactly one byte: 0x00 represents FALSE and 0x01 represents TRUE. All other values are invalid. A Boolean flag never occupies an individual bit.

chunk_8.page_content:
## 2.4 Numeric and Text Encoding

Integer widths and byte order are specified per field. Unless stated otherwise, multi-byte integers are little-endian. ASCII and UTF-8 fields shall use their named encodings. Text lengths are measured in encoded bytes.

chunk_9.page_content:
## 2.5 Packet Boundaries

A packet may occur at the beginning, middle, or end of a larger transport payload. Packet boundaries are determined by the signature, length fields, count fields, or other framing rules in the relevant definition. One TCP payload is not assumed to equal one application packet.

chunk_10.page_content:
## 2.6 Reserved Values and Validation

Reserved bytes shall be zero. Enumerations shall contain only listed values. Receivers shall reject invalid lengths, unsupported enumeration values, invalid Boolean encodings, and failed checksums where specified.

chunk_13.page_content:
### 3.1.1 Packet Overview

Sender: GUI Subsystem. Receiver: ZYNQ Control Subsystem. Flow Direction: GUI Subsystem → ZYNQ Control Subsystem. This fixed-length packet carries a user-selected command and numeric argument.

chunk_14.page_content:
### 3.1.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Start Marker 4 ASCII Exact value: GUI!.
Command ID 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer 0 = STOP; 1 = START; 2 = RESET; 3 = SET_LEVEL.
Enable 1 Boolean 0x00 = FALSE; 0x01 = TRUE.
Command Argument 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Valid range: 0–1000.
Transaction ID 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Valid range: 0–65535.
End Marker 4 ASCII Exact value: !END.

chunk_15.page_content:
### 3.1.3 Length and Validation

The packet shall be exactly 14 bytes. Start Marker occupies offsets 0–3 and End Marker offsets 10–13. Command ID shall be defined, Enable shall be 0x00 or 0x01, and Command Argument shall not exceed 1000.

chunk_17.page_content:
### 3.2.1 Packet Overview

Sender: ZYNQ Control Subsystem. Receiver: Mission Dashboard Subsystem. Flow Direction: ZYNQ Control Subsystem → Mission Dashboard Subsystem. This fixed-length packet reports a sample counter, temperature, supply voltage, and sensor health.

chunk_18.page_content:
### 3.2.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Signature 4 ASCII Exact value: TLM1.
Sample Counter 4 Unsigned 32-bit, little-endian 0–4294967295.
Temperature 2 Signed 16-bit, little-endian Tenths of °C; range -400 to 1250.
Supply Voltage 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Millivolts; range 0–60000.
Sensor Healthy 1 Boolean 0x00 = FALSE; 0x01 = TRUE.
Operating Mode 1 Unsigned 8-bit enumeration 0 = OFFLINE; 1 = STANDBY; 2 = ACTIVE; 3 = MAINTENANCE.
Reserved 2 Byte array Both bytes shall be 0x00.

chunk_19.page_content:
### 3.2.3 Length and Validation

The packet shall be exactly 16 bytes. Signature shall equal TLM1. Numeric values shall be in range, Sensor Healthy shall be a valid Boolean, Operating Mode shall be defined, and Reserved bytes shall be zero.

chunk_21.page_content:
### 3.3.1 Packet Overview

Sender: Data Archive Subsystem. Receiver: Storage Gateway Subsystem. Flow Direction: Data Archive Subsystem → Storage Gateway Subsystem. This variable-length packet transfers a named archive object; its content may be empty.

chunk_22.page_content:
### 3.3.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Signature 3 ASCII Exact value: ARC.
Object Name Length 1 Unsigned 8-bit Number of bytes in Object Name; 1–64.
Object Name Object Name Length UTF-8 Valid UTF-8; shall not contain a zero byte.
Content Length 4 Unsigned 32-bit, little-endian Number of Content bytes; zero permitted.
Content Content Length Byte array Opaque; any byte value permitted.
Transfer Complete 1 Boolean 0x00 = FALSE; 0x01 = TRUE.

chunk_23.page_content:
### 3.3.3 Variable-Length Validation

Total length shall equal 9 + Object Name Length + Content Length bytes. Object Name Length shall be 1–64. Content Length may be zero. Transfer Complete shall be 0x00 or 0x01. Truncated packets and trailing bytes shall be rejected.

chunk_25.page_content:
### 3.4.1 Packet Overview

Sender: Route Planner Subsystem. Receiver: Autonomous Vehicle Subsystem. Flow Direction: Route Planner Subsystem → Autonomous Vehicle Subsystem. This fixed-length packet communicates a waypoint, coordinates, and movement preference.

chunk_26.page_content:
### 3.4.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Signature 4 ASCII Exact value: NAVI.
Waypoint ID 2 Unsigned 16-bit, big-endian 1–65535.
Latitude 4 Signed 32-bit, big-endian Degrees × 10^6; -90000000 to 90000000.
Longitude 4 Signed 32-bit, big-endian Degrees × 10^6; -180000000 to 180000000.
Use Preferred Route 1 Boolean 0x00 = FALSE; 0x01 = TRUE.
Movement Profile 1 Unsigned 8-bit enumeration 0 = NORMAL; 1 = QUIET; 2 = FAST; 3 = CONSERVATIVE.
Reserved 2 Byte array Both bytes shall be 0x00.

chunk_27.page_content:
### 3.4.3 Length and Validation

The packet shall be exactly 18 bytes. Signature shall equal NAVI. Coordinates shall be in range. Use Preferred Route shall be 0x00 or 0x01. Movement Profile shall be defined and Reserved bytes shall be zero.

chunk_29.page_content:
### 3.5.1 Packet Overview

Sender: Spectrometer Subsystem. Receiver: Experiment Orchestrator Subsystem. Flow Direction: Spectrometer Subsystem → Experiment Orchestrator Subsystem. This variable-length packet contains a result identifier and a count-controlled sequence of measurement records.

chunk_30.page_content:
### 3.5.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Signature 4 ASCII Exact value: LABR.
Result ID 4 Unsigned 32-bit, big-endian 0–4294967295.
Measurement Count 1 Unsigned 8-bit Number of records; 0–20.
Measurement Records Count × 5 Repeated structure Exactly Count records follow.
Channel ID (per record) 1 Unsigned 8-bit 0–31.
Measured Value (per record) 2 Signed 16-bit, big-endian Thousandths of configured unit.
Measurement Valid (per record) 1 Boolean 0x00 = FALSE; 0x01 = TRUE.
Quality Code (per record) 1 Unsigned 8-bit enumeration 0 = UNKNOWN; 1 = ACCEPTABLE; 2 = SUSPECT; 3 = INVALID.
Batch Accepted 1 Boolean 0x00 = FALSE; 0x01 = TRUE.

chunk_31.page_content:
### 3.5.3 Repeated Record and Length Validation

Total length shall equal 10 + (Measurement Count × 5) bytes. Count may be zero, producing a 10-byte packet with no records. Each record is exactly five bytes. Channel ID and Quality Code shall be valid, and all Boolean values shall be 0x00 or 0x01.

chunk_32.page_content:
# 4 Cross-Packet Interface Summary
Packet Sender Receiver Direction Length
GUI Command GUI Subsystem ZYNQ Control GUI → ZYNQ 14 bytes
Telemetry Snapshot ZYNQ Control Mission Dashboard ZYNQ → Dashboard 16 bytes
Archive Transfer Data Archive Storage Gateway Archive → Gateway Variable
Navigation Intent Route Planner Autonomous Vehicle Planner → Vehicle 18 bytes
Laboratory Result Spectrometer Experiment Orchestrator Spectrometer → Orchestrator Variable

chunk_34.page_content:
## 5.1 Fixed-Length Packets

GUI Command is 14 bytes, Telemetry Snapshot is 16 bytes, and Navigation Intent is 18 bytes. Each requires exact-length validation and packet-specific value checks.

chunk_35.page_content:
## 5.2 Variable-Length Packets

Archive Transfer length is derived from Object Name Length and Content Length. Laboratory Result length is derived from Measurement Count. Receivers shall calculate expected lengths and reject incomplete or overlong candidates.

chunk_36.page_content:
## 5.3 Direction Validation

Packet identity includes sender and receiver. An analyzer should retain observed source and destination endpoints and verify direction against configured subsystem-to-endpoint mappings. A byte-pattern match alone does not prove correct flow direction.

chunk_37.page_content:
# 6 Document Notes

This is an illustrative IRS for testing document extraction, structured schema generation, and packet-pattern detection. All fields are byte-aligned; no bit-packed fields are used. Every Boolean flag occupies one full byte. Packet examples are intentionally diverse and need not form a coherent real-world system.
